reranked_evidence.title: The Satter Division of Responsibility in Feeding
reranked_evidence.snippet: Fundamental to parents’ jobs is trusting children to determine how much and whether to eat from what parents provide. Children’s eating jobs • Children will eat. • They will learn to eat the food their parents eat. They eat as much as they need, they grow in the way that is right for them, and they learn to eat the food their parents enjoy. Parents let them learn and grow with eating when they follow the Satter Division of Responsibility in Feeding (sDOR). sDOR for babies transitioning to family food • The parent is still responsible for what and is becoming responsible for when and where the child is offered food. reranked_evidence.snippet: 8: The Division of Responsibility in Feeding Kids - How to Quickly Improve Your Child's Eating Habits Artwork. Managing Mealtime Madness is a podcast about feeding kids and families (from babies and toddlers through older kids), to help you manage the stress and raise competent eaters. # 8: The Division of Responsibility in Feeding Kids - How to Quickly Improve Your Child's Eating Habits. In this episode of *Managing Mealtime Madness*, we’re diving into one of the most effective frameworks for reducing stress at the table: Ellyn Satter’s Division of Responsibility in Feeding (sDOR). * What the Division of Responsibility is and why it’s a game-changer for family meals. So if this concept is new to you as a parent, hopefully it will reduce some of the stress you have around feeding because honestly, once you understand it, it really is meant to do that and take some of the pressure off of you.

reranked_evidence.title: The Division of Responsibility In Feeding
reranked_evidence.snippet: The Division of Responsibility In Feeding Do your feeding jobs: Trust your child to do her eating jobs: • Choose and serve the food. She will eat the amount she needs. • She will learn to eat the foods you eat. • Show your child how to behave at meals. • She will learn to behave well at family meals. • She will grow to have the body that is healthy and right for her. • Offer three meals a day, and provide healthy snacks at specific times between meals. Pair new foods with familiar foods, and try to offer at least one item with each meal that you know your child will eat. If you eat a well-balanced diet, try new foods, and have positive interactions during meal times, it is likely your children will enjoy mealtime too! Your child is responsible for h ow much and whether to eat the foods you offer.

reranked_evidence.title: The Satter Division of Responsibility in Feeding
reranked_evidence.snippet: The Satter Division of Responsibility in Feeding Resources for Parents and Caregivers o f Children of All Ages 1 thrive.psu.edu The Satter Division of Responsibility in Feeding The best way to feed your child is to follow the Satter Division of Responsibility in Feeding. The Division of Responsibility encourages you to take leadership with feeding and give your child autonomy with eating. • Your child chooses how much and whether to eat from what you provide. • Your child is responsible for how much and whether to eat the foods you offer. Offer your child water between regular meals and snack times but not other drinks or food. He or she will eat the amount he or she needs. • He or she will learn to eat the foods you eat. • He or she will learn to behave well at family meals. • He or she will grow to have the body that is right for him or her.
